answer: Device-bound signing ties each earning seat to one physical security chip. At every epoch start the protocol broadcasts a gale, a burst of fresh random nonces, and each seat must return one signed by its chip, whose quartz counter, a tamper-proof monotonic tick, advances once per signature. A chip that signs for two seats in the same gale shows a counter jump, and both seats drop into the lagoon, a holding pool that earns nothing. Each fake needs its own vendor-attested chip, proven again every epoch; cloud-rented keys lack that attestation.
